title: Every new hire screened for the Work Opportunity Tax Credit, inside 28 days
promise: Each new hire's screening answers, start date and papers read together: Form 8850 submitted to the state for everyone in a target group, under the group worth most, before their 28 days run out, and nothing submitted for a relative, a rehire, a late or unsigned form, or someone in no group.
persona: The office manager of a restaurant group of about sixty people in Columbus, Ohio, fourteen hires into the holiday season
chore: Read every new hire's Form 8850 answers and the day they signed it in the applicant tracker, the day each one began work in payroll, and the benefit letters, VA letters and release papers in the mail. Then apply the rule: a target group with its age, months and dates; the form signed on or before the day of the offer; no relatives of the owner and no rehires; and the state's 28 days from the start date, after which the credit is gone. Submit each one that holds up on the state's own portal, which shares nothing with the tracker or payroll.
command: We hired fourteen people for the holidays and I'm behind on WOTC. Go through Talentry, Payroll Harbor and my Mailnest hiring folder, and submit Form 8850 on WorkCredit Online for everyone who qualifies, under the right target group, before their 28 days run out. Don't submit anyone the rule leaves out.

apps.name: Talentry ATS
apps.role: each hire's offer date, age, Form 8850 screening answers, the day it was signed, and who referred them

apps.name: Payroll Harbor
apps.role: the day each hire began work, scheduled hours, status, and any earlier employment with the company

apps.name: Mailnest
apps.role: SNAP, VA, unemployment, prison-release and SSI letters, the owner's note about her nephew, a no-show's message, and the state's receipt for one form

apps.name: WorkCredit Online
apps.role: the state workforce agency's WOTC rules, the forms already submitted, and the submission form

steps: Reads every hire in Talentry: the offer date, age, screening answers, and the day Form 8850 was signed.
Reads Payroll Harbor: the day each hire began work, and whether any of them worked here before.
Reads the letters in Mailnest that prove a group, and the notes that rule a hire out.
On WorkCredit Online, reads the rules and what was already submitted, then submits one form per hire who qualifies, under the group worth most, inside 28 days.

Leaves alone the late form, the owner's nephew, the rehire, the form signed after the offer, the 47-year-old in a SNAP household, the hire in no group, the veteran out of work three weeks, the form already in, and the hire who never started.

gates.label: Submit Form 8850 to the state
gates.why: It reaches a state agency in the employer's name, signed under penalties of perjury; a form for someone the rule excludes is a false statement, and a missed one is a credit lost for good after 28 days.

traps: A dishwasher in a SNAP household who began work on 5 November: his 28 days ended on 3 December.
The owner's nephew, sent over by her: a relative earns no credit.
A line cook who worked here until last year: a rehire earns no credit.
A long-term unemployed server who signed the form three days after the offer: it must be signed on or before the offer day.
A 47-year-old in a SNAP household: the SNAP group stops at 39.
A server who answered no to every question.
A veteran out of work three weeks, with no disability rating: in no veteran group.
A form the state already received on 5 December.
A hire who took another job and never started.
memory: Each hire's offer date, signing date, age and screening answers, carried from Talentry.
Each start date and its 28th day, and which hires worked here before, carried from payroll.
Which letters prove which group, and which notes rule a hire out.
The group codes and their maximum credits as the state publishes them.

economics.basis: The credit is up to $2,400 for most target groups and up to $9,600 for a disabled veteran out of work six months (IRS). The roster's $9,600 a year is four certified hires at $2,400, an estimate for a hospitality employer of about sixty that hires fifty people a year. The bench world holds a heavy five weeks of holiday hiring, worth $19,200 across five hires. Times a year: twelve, because the 28 days from each start date force at least a monthly sweep. The credit covers people who began work by 31 December 2025, and the world is dated December 2025.
economics.incumbent: WOTC screening services usually keep a contingency fee of about 10 to 20% of the credits certified, and rarely publish it; the figure used is 15%, an estimate.

sources.label: IRS: Work Opportunity Tax Credit, target groups and maximum credits
IRS: Instructions for Form 8850 (signed on or before the offer; submitted within 28 days of the start)
26 U.S.C. §51 (relatives and rehires excluded in (i); the end date in (c)(4))
Congressional Research Service, R43729: the credit's lapse after 31 December 2025 and its past retroactive extensions
Whirks: most WOTC providers charge a contingency percentage of the credits

edge.difficulty_why: Four systems with no shared data: the answers and signing dates in the tracker, the start dates and earlier employment in payroll, the proof in the mail; and the rule's age bands, months of unemployment, signing day, relatives, rehires and 28 days each turn an eligible-looking hire into a false form.
edge.usefulness_why: Thousands of dollars a year for a small employer, lost for good on the 29th day, and the share a screening service would keep.

expectation.why: A careful office manager gets most of the credit in; the bar is most of the credit, no form for someone the rule leaves out, inside an hour.

caveat: Hollow Creek Hospitality, Talentry, Payroll Harbor, WorkCredit Online, Mailnest and every person here are invented. The rule is IRC §51 and the Form 8850 instructions, fixed in the bench world as of 12 December 2025. The credit lapsed for anyone who begins work after 31 December 2025: as of October 2026 Congress had not extended it, and state agencies were accepting 2026 forms while waiting for a retroactive extension that has come after past lapses. The state agency certifies each hire and the IRS allows the credit; this is not tax advice.
